newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slammed as PC fears spark sell-off in techs.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slammed as PC fears spark sell-off in techs.

text.p: Fears of soft personal computer sales dealt a crushing blow on Monday to the Nasdaq Composite Index as investors rushed to unload technology stocks in a wave of late selling.

The Nasdaq Composite Index lost almost two percent, spiralling down 23.81 to 1261 in late trading, the sharpest drop since a 32 point loss on July 23. The Dow sank 36 to 6268 and the long bond fell 24/32 to yield 6.63 percent.
Fears were heightened after Circuit City Stores Inc posted weak results and said third=quarter personal computers sales were dramatically softer. Shares fell 1-1/4 to 29-3/4.

"Everyone's nervous in general ever since Greenspan," one trader said, referring to comments made by the Fed chairman. "The market's been very choppy and especially the Nasdaq because it's so momentum oriented. Once sellers come in, everyone follows the pack," he said.
Blue chip technology stocks suffered. Intel Corp shares fell 5-1/8 to 127-1/4, Microsoft Corp fell 3-1/4 to 76-3/4, Oracle Corp fell 1-7/16 to 42-9/16, and Dell Computer Corp fell 2-3/4 to 54-3/8.
Losing stocks beat gainers by 2590 to 1676 on volume of about 530 million shares.
